create.name: Ajahn Brahm
create.bio:
Ajahn Brahm is a Theravāda Buddhist monk of the Thai forest tradition and abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery at Serpentine, in the hills south of Perth. Born Peter Betts in London in 1951, he read theoretical physics at Cambridge and taught for a year before travelling to Thailand, where he was ordained in 1974 and spent nine years training under Ajahn Chah. Sent to Perth in 1983, he helped to build Bodhinyana largely by hand and is the spiritual head of the Buddhist Society of Western Australia. In 2009 he helped hold the first bhikkhuni ordination in his branch of the forest tradition, which led the wider Ajahn Chah network to cut ties with him; in 2019 he received the Medal of the Order of Australia for services to Buddhism and gender equality.

He is known for teaching through stories and gentle humour, and for presenting deep stillness and the jhānas as within reach of ordinary practitioners. His books include Kindfulness, The Art of Disappearing, Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond, and Opening the Door of Your Heart, a collection of teaching stories also sold as Who Ordered This Truckload of Dung? In Perth he gives Friday evening talks and Saturday guided sittings at the Dhammaloka centre in Nollamara, streamed live on YouTube, and he leads retreats and talks overseas most years.

courses.title: A Mind Like a Still Forest Pool: Non-Residential Weekend Retreat with Ajahn Brahm & Ajahn Canda
courses.description: A two-day weekend retreat in Oxford, taught with Ajahn Canda during his November 2026 UK visit, with guided sittings, talks and time for questions. Lunch and tea breaks are included and you go home each evening.

free_resources.title: Guided Meditation by Ajahn Brahm
free_resources.description: The Buddhist Society of Western Australia's library of his recorded guided sittings, most taken from the Saturday sessions in Perth. Free to stream, and a good way into his relaxed, step-by-step style.

free_resources.title: Meditation Retreats by Ajahn Brahm
free_resources.description: Recordings from the retreats he has led, with the talks and instructions given day by day. Useful for anyone who wants to follow a full retreat's teaching at home.

free_resources.title: Friday Night Speaker – Ajahn Brahm
free_resources.description: His regular Friday evening at the Dhammaloka centre in Nollamara: chanting, a half-hour guided meditation and an hour-long Dhamma talk. Open to all at no charge and streamed live on the society's YouTube channel.

sprint.tier_evidence: No personal accounts found: the YouTube channel his talks appear on is the Buddhist Society of Western Australia's (@BuddhistSocietyWA, 222K subscribers from its own header, 3 Nov 2026), a shared organisation account that is not counted; Facebook/Twitter links on bswa.org are also the society's, and facebook.com was not opened → 0 personal followers readable → local_hero by count
sprint.tier_override: Editorial stature: author of internationally published books with Wisdom Publications (Opening the Door of Your Heart / Who Ordered This Truckload of Dung?, Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond, Kindfulness), translated widely; founding abbot of Bodhinyana and spiritual director of the BSWA, whose teachings the society says are heard by millions online. Proposed luminary; owner decides (could be argued higher).
flags: Base: he lives at Bodhinyana Monastery, 216 Kingsbury Drive, Serpentine WA (BSWA contact page); Serpentine is a small town in the Shire of Serpentine-Jarrahdale on Perth's south-eastern edge (~50 km from the CBD) and may need a place alias to Perth for Near You. His weekly Perth teaching is at Dhammaloka, Nollamara.

Email admin@bswa.org is the Buddhist Society of WA's general office inbox, not a personal address; BSWA's 'Contact a monastic' page also routes questions via SuttaCentral's forum and in-person visits.
Tier: 0 personal followers readable (all channels are BSWA's); luminary proposed via tier_override for editorial stature. Owner decides; superhero could also be argued.

Books left out: wisdomexperience.org (Wisdom Publications, his publisher) returned a Cloudflare challenge on robots.txt, so it was skipped; no teacher or publisher page with ISBNs could be read (BSWA bookshop lists titles without ISBNs). Wikipedia lists ISBNs (e.g. 0861712757, 086171668X, 9781614291992) but is not a teacher/publisher source. Owner may want to add his books.

Videos are on the BSWA channel (shared), chosen from its Live tab with him as sole speaker; titles kept as published, including '| Ajahn Brahm | date'. youtube_url left null because the channel is the society's.
The Oxford weekend retreat is co-taught with Ajahn Canda, who is already on Spiritpedia (ajahn-canda); organised by the Anukampa Bhikkhuni Project, not BSWA.

Photo: only the Wikimedia Commons portrait is used; the BSWA teacher-page photo (AB-dhammatalk-420px.png) closed the connection to the ingest photo check (UND_ERR_SOCKET), so it was dropped, not retried.
Not an Insight Timer check: insighttimer.com profiles render by script and could not be read.
Wikipedia notes he was removed from the Ajahn Chah forest sangha network after the 2009 bhikkhuni ordination; the bio mentions this neutrally. A human may prefer to drop it.
left_out: All books (see flags): no readable teacher/publisher page with ISBNs; wisdomexperience.org behind a Cloudflare challenge.
'The Bliss of Enlightenment' eight-day residential retreat at Gaunts House, Dorset (13 to 20 Nov 2026): fully booked, registration closed.
Evening talks in Oxford (10 Nov), Croydon (24 Nov) and London (25 Nov 2026): single evening events.
Ajahn Brahm retreat in Malaysia (19 Dec 2026 to 1 Jan 2027): organised by the Buddhist Gem Fellowship; no programme page or price read.
Guided Meditation streams on YouTube: kept as the free BSWA library rather than as single videos; birthday, auction and chanting streams are not teaching.
